# Production Bar — warleyd-client-template

> What "production grade" means for **warleyd-client-template** in 2026, expressed as a checklist of yes/no observations. This is the loop-mode exit condition: aider (or any AI assistant) loops until every checked-applicable item is true. Items are anchored to canonical references — Laws of UX, Nielsen heuristics, WCAG 2.2 AA, Core Web Vitals 2026, OWASP ASVS L1 — so a failure can be justified by *why*, not just *that*.

**Surface:** client-template
**Stack:** astro · tailwind · islands
**Perf profile:** marketing-page (budgets in §4)
**Identity overrides:** see `./VISION.md` §4 Look & Feel for what makes *this* product visually and emotionally distinctive on top of this bar.

---

## 1. The Bar (in plain English)

warleyd-client-template ships at the quality level a 2026 user expects from Stripe, Linear, modern agency landing pages. That means: every tap feels instant, nothing is ever a blank wall, every flow has a visible beginning / middle / end, the app works for people on screen readers and people who reduced their motion, and the design system is consistent enough that a stranger could draw the next screen without seeing it. This file is not a wish list — it is the gate. A feature is not done if it is not green here.

---

## 2. Laws of UX — applied

Each law is mapped to one or two enforceable, yes/no checks. Cite the law name in code review when something fails.

- [ ] **Jakob's Law** — Reactions, share, comment, follow, sign-in use platform-native patterns. A user from Instagram / Airbnb / BlueSky / LinkedIn recognizes them without thinking.
- [ ] **Fitts's Law** — Primary CTAs are ≥ 44×44 CSS px (mobile) / ≥ 32×32 (desktop). Destructive actions are NOT placed adjacent to primary CTAs without spacing.
- [ ] **Hick's Law** — Primary screens show ≤ 5 actions at first paint. Power options are behind progressive disclosure (menus, settings, "more"), not on the surface.
- [ ] **Miller's Law** — Lists of controls or filters are grouped in chunks of ≤ 7 visible items.
- [ ] **Doherty Threshold** — Every user input produces a visible response in < 400ms. Where the round-trip is slower, the UI is optimistic (visible change first, server confirms or rolls back).
- [ ] **Peak-End Rule** — The peak and the end of each Core Flow (see VISION.md §3) are identified in code comments or design notes, and have received explicit polish (animation, copy, confirmation).
- [ ] **Aesthetic-Usability Effect** — Components use design-system tokens for color / spacing / radius / shadow. No raw hex codes outside the token file. No magic numbers for spacing.
- [ ] **Tesler's Law** — Inherent complexity is moved out of the user's path: sensible defaults, server-side derivation, smart autocomplete — not extra form fields.
- [ ] **Goal-Gradient Effect** — Any flow > 2 steps has a visible progress indicator (stepper, progress bar, "step 2 of 4").
- [ ] **Postel's Law** — Forms accept loose input (trim whitespace, normalize phone/email casing, accept multiple date formats). Server output is strict and canonical.
- [ ] **Serial Position Effect** — Most-important nav / list items are at the start or end of lists, not buried in the middle.
- [ ] **Von Restorff (Isolation Effect)** — Exactly one primary CTA per screen. Secondary actions are visually subordinate, not competing.

---

## 3. Nielsen 10 Usability Heuristics — applied

- [ ] **Visibility of system status** — Every async operation shows a state from {loading, empty, error, success}. See §5 for the four-states contract.
- [ ] **Match between system and the real world** — Copy uses the user's vocabulary, not engineering vocabulary. No "fetch", "endpoint", "payload", "token expired" without translation.
- [ ] **User control & freedom** — Destructive actions are confirmable AND undoable where possible (toast with "undo" for ≥ 5s, or restore-from-trash within 30 days for permanent deletion).
- [ ] **Consistency & standards** — A reaction / share / bookmark / comment works identically wherever it appears (feed, detail, drawer, modal).
- [ ] **Error prevention** — Destructive actions require confirmation. Forms validate before submit. Mutually exclusive options are disabled, not just shown as errors after.
- [ ] **Recognition over recall** — Autocomplete on inputs where the answer space is bounded (cities, tags, users). Recently-used items surface first.
- [ ] **Flexibility & efficiency** — Power flows have keyboard shortcuts (`/` to search, `Esc` to close, `Enter` to submit, `Cmd/Ctrl+K` for command palette where applicable).
- [ ] **Aesthetic & minimalist** — One primary action per screen (see Von Restorff above). No competing visual weight.
- [ ] **Error recovery** — Every error message names the recovery action ("Check your connection and try again" not "Network error"). Error states include a retry button where retry makes sense.
- [ ] **Help & documentation** — Contextual help (tooltips, inline hints) where actions are non-obvious. Not buried in a separate help center.

## 4. Performance — Core Web Vitals 2026 (marketing-page budget)

- [ ] **LCP** < 1.5s p75 on mid-tier mobile, < 1.0s on desktop
- [ ] **INP** < 200ms p75
- [ ] **CLS** < 0.05 (stricter — no shift from late hero / banner)
- [ ] **TTFB** < 400ms p75 (static or edge-rendered)
- [ ] **JS bundle (initial)** ≤ 100KB gz

- [ ] **JS bundle (initial)** — within budget above, gzipped. Code-split anything > 50KB that isn't on the critical path.
- [ ] **Images** — Lazy-loaded below the fold. Responsive `srcset` or `<picture>`. Modern format (AVIF / WebP) with fallback. No layout shift on load (explicit width/height or `aspect-ratio`).
- [ ] **Fonts** — Self-hosted or preloaded with `font-display: swap`. ≤ 2 font families. ≤ 4 weights.
- [ ] **Lists** — Lists > 20 items are virtualized.
- [ ] **Queries** — No N+1 in the data path. Server batches related fetches. Client prefetches adjacent data (next page, hover-prefetch on links).
- [ ] **Third-party scripts** — Each one earns its place. Analytics deferred. Tag managers off the critical path.

---

## 5. The Four States (every async surface)

For every screen / component that loads data or accepts input:

- [ ] **Loading** — Skeleton matches the final layout's dimensions (no layout shift on resolve). Skeleton is NOT a spinner over a blank wall.
- [ ] **Empty** — Has an illustration or icon, an explanation in plain language, a primary CTA to populate the state, and (when applicable) a secondary action ("import", "invite", "explore").
- [ ] **Error** — Names the failure category, names the recovery action, offers a retry button where retry is meaningful. Never blames the user. Never just says "Error".
- [ ] **Success** — The new state is visibly confirmed (item appears in list, count updates, toast with action verb). Optimistic where the action is reversible.

**No dead ends.** A scrollable surface never just stops — at the bottom, show suggested content, related items, or an engaging "you're caught up" with what to do next.

---

## 6. Accessibility Floor — WCAG 2.2 AA (non-negotiable)

- [ ] **Contrast** — Text ≥ 4.5:1 (≥ 3:1 for large text ≥ 18pt). UI components and graphical objects ≥ 3:1.
- [ ] **Keyboard** — Every interactive element reachable by Tab. Focus order is logical. Visible focus ring (not removed by `outline: none` without replacement).
- [ ] **Names** — Every interactive element has an accessible name (visible label, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`). Icon-only buttons MUST have an accessible name.
- [ ] **Semantics** — Use semantic HTML (`<button>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<h1>`–`<h6>` in order). ARIA only adds what semantics can't express.
- [ ] **Screen reader** — Primary flows audited with VoiceOver (iOS / macOS) or TalkBack (Android) or NVDA (Windows). Announcements for async state changes.
- [ ] **Reduced motion** — `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` short-circuits non-essential animation to a fade or instant transition.
- [ ] **Target size** — Touch targets ≥ 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 — 2.5.8). Prefer ≥ 44×44 for primary actions.
- [ ] **Forms** — Every input has a programmatic label. Errors are linked to inputs via `aria-describedby`. Required fields are programmatically required, not just visually marked.
- [ ] **Color is not the only signal** — Errors / status / required-ness uses an icon or text in addition to color.

---

## 7. Visual System & Motion

- [ ] **Spacing** — 8pt (or 4pt) grid. Spacing values come from a token set.
- [ ] **Type** — Defined type scale (e.g., 12/14/16/18/24/32/48). No off-scale sizes.
- [ ] **Tokens** — Color, radius, shadow, motion (easing + duration) come from the design system. No raw hex / px values outside the token file.
- [ ] **Dark mode** — At parity with light mode. Every screen tested in both.
- [ ] **Motion** — Entrance < 250ms, exit < 200ms. Easing from the token set. No layout-shifting animation. Reduced-motion path exists.
- [ ] **Iconography** — One icon set, consistent stroke weight and corner style.

---

## 8. Forms (Postel + Tesler + Error prevention)

- [ ] Validate on blur (not on every keystroke). Show success state when valid.
- [ ] Server errors map to specific fields (not just a generic banner).
- [ ] `autocomplete` attributes correct (`email`, `current-password`, `new-password`, `one-time-code`, `street-address`, `postal-code`, `tel`, `cc-number`).
- [ ] Optimistic submit where the action is reversible.
- [ ] Autosave for flows > 3 fields. Visible save indicator.
- [ ] Input normalization on the way in (trim, lowercase email, strip spaces from phone) — Postel's Law.
- [ ] Confirmation only on actions that are destructive or expensive.

---

## 9. Trust, Privacy, Safety — OWASP ASVS L1 signals

- [ ] **Privacy / terms** reachable from any screen (footer, settings).
- [ ] **Data deletion** is self-serve and visible (not a support ticket).
- [ ] **Auth flows** preview the next step ("we'll send you a code", "you'll be redirected back here").
- [ ] **No dark patterns** — no confirmshaming, no opt-out-by-default for paid features, no hidden subscription renewals, no fake urgency.
- [ ] **Destructive actions** are confirmable and reversible where possible (soft-delete, undo).
- [ ] **Session handling** — sessions expire predictably, expiry is communicated, re-auth is friction-light.
- [ ] **Sensitive actions** (email change, password change, payment method) require recent auth or step-up auth.

---

## 10. Content & Copy

- [ ] Active voice, present tense, sentence case in UI strings.
- [ ] Error messages name the recovery, not just the failure.
- [ ] No engineering jargon in user-facing text.
- [ ] Empty states sound like a person wrote them.
- [ ] (this project is single-locale; i18n block omitted.)

## Marketing Page Conversion Patterns

- [ ] Above-the-fold renders in < 1.0s LCP on mid-tier mobile. Hero image is the LCP element and is preloaded.
- [ ] Primary CTA is visible without scrolling on mobile (≤ 700px viewport). Repeats every ~2 viewport heights as the user scrolls.
- [ ] Social proof appears within the first viewport on the home / landing page — logos, testimonial, count, or rating. Real, not placeholder.
- [ ] Forms ask for the minimum necessary information. Email-only capture forms for top-of-funnel; richer forms only after value is shown.
- [ ] Form submission produces a visible success state on the same page — no jarring redirect to a "thanks" page unless required for tracking, in which case the redirect is < 500ms.
- [ ] Lead magnets (PDF, demo, free trial) deliver instantly via on-screen download or inline email — never "we'll get back to you within 24 hours" for an automated artifact.
- [ ] Cookie / consent banner is small, non-modal, and remembers the choice. No banner over the CTA.
- [ ] All outbound links from the marketing site preserve UTM-style attribution where it matters.
- [ ] Open Graph + Twitter card meta tags ship on every page with a distinct title + description + image. Tested via the relevant social debugger.
- [ ] Sitemap.xml and robots.txt exist and are correct. Canonical URLs on every page. Schema.org JSON-LD for Organization (and Product / Article / FAQ where applicable).
- [ ] No layout shift after font load. No layout shift from cookie banner mounting.

## 11. Loop-Mode Operating Contract (for aider, Claude, Ralph)

If you are an AI assistant running in a loop against this checklist, this section is binding.

1. **Objective format.** The human states the objective as a subset of items from §§ 2–10 ("bring screen X to items #12–#17"). You do not invent items.
2. **One item per iteration.** Pick the *next unchecked applicable* item. Make the *smallest* change that satisfies it.
3. **Test after every iteration.** Run `test-cmd` from `.aider.conf.yml`. If green, mark the item satisfied in your notes and move on. If red, fix the regression OR revert — never both at once.
4. **Stop conditions.** Exit the loop when:
   - All applicable items are green, OR
   - The same item has failed 3× consecutively (escalate to the human), OR
   - `test-cmd` has regressed on a previously-green item (escalate).
5. **Read-only docs.** You may NOT edit `VISION.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `PRODUCTION_BAR.md`, or `.aider.conf.yml`. You MAY append a single paragraph to `AIDER_NOTES.md` per iteration with: timestamp, item attempted, outcome (passed / deferred / blocked), short note.
6. **No scope creep.** You do NOT add items to this checklist. Only the human does.
7. **Diff budget.** Soft cap ~400 changed lines per iteration. Over that, split the change into multiple iterations.
8. **Cite the law.** When you mark an item satisfied, name the law / heuristic in your `AIDER_NOTES.md` entry ("Doherty Threshold: added optimistic update on reaction click, falls back on 5xx").
